content: Nature gave us one tongue and two ears, so we could hear twice as much as we speak.
author: Zeno of Citium
sourceWork: Fragments of the Early Stoa (c. 300 BC)
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Water is the softest thing on earth, yet it carves through solid granite. It doesn't fight obstacles; it yields, flows around them, and quietly finds its way to its natural level.

In Zeno of Citium's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. When we force outcomes with brute willpower and anxiety, we exhaust ourselves and create unnecessary resistance. Aligning with nature means trusting the timing of things and moving with steady, patient persistence.
reflectionPrompt: In what area of your life are you overthinking the ideal approach instead of taking the simple, honorable action?
